The Government of Canada knowingly expanded MAID via Bill C-7 (2021), removing the “reasonably foreseeable death” safeguard. Rome Statute Article 6(a) forbids killing members of an identifiable group with intent to destroy that group in whole or in part. The intent is on the parliamentary record.
The documentary stage below stitches the ACT I chapter film. Then walk the evidence scene-by-scene. Atmosphere is not the proof; Hansard and Health Canada are.
Each beat carries a still or film layer behind the text. Stats open charts when the evidence is numeric. Reduced-motion devices get stills only.
The gallery is a reading board: documentary stills and atmospheric loops set tone; charts summarize government series. Open each act for the cited numbers.
Atmosphere for the parliamentary frame. The primary path is Hansard and the statute text of Bill C-7.
Lametti on second reading: eligibility expands by removing reasonably foreseeable natural death. The quote is on the record.
5.1% of all deaths in Canada administered through MAID in 2024 — Health Canada Fifth Annual Report. The curve is the expansion after C-7.
Death not reasonably foreseeable — the cohort C-7 created. About 776 Canadians in 2024. Same MAID volume series as the federal report (not a multi-cause attrition composite).
Memorial atmosphere for the clinical path — not a case file. The volume and eligibility rules sit in Health Canada tables and the Criminal Code amendments.
C-7 was debated and passed with explicit awareness that removing the safeguard would route disabled, chronically ill, and economically vulnerable people into a state death program.
Background film and stills set memorial tone. They do not establish intent. Intent is argued from Hansard , the statute , and the annual MAID reports that quantify who dies under Track 2.
Article 6(a) is a legal frame for reading the public record — not a court verdict. TENET5 cites primary documents so you can check every claim.
